source_meta.reported_context: An adult young woman from Gaza City recounts being given the choice to view the bodies of her parents and sister after they were martyred, despite being warned that the bodies were charred and difficult to recognize. She decides to see them because she had previously not seen or farewelled her martyred siblings and did not want to carry the same hasra. She describes the horror of seeing burned and fragmented bodies, then ends with hamd and a martyrdom frame.
source_meta.collection_context_en: The speaker describes being warned that the bodies were charred and may not be recognizable, then being asked whether she still wanted to see them. She refuses to avoid the scene, saying that whatever their condition, they are her parents and sister, and that she already carries the regret of not seeing and not farewelling her previously martyred siblings. She then describes the sight as terrifying and almost beyond words. Her sister, who had been in the car with them, had no recognizable trace and appeared as pieces/remains. Her mother’s face was burned. She remembers her father as a dignified, beautiful man with presence, and contrasts that memory with the state in which she saw him. The narrative ends with 'الحمدلله' and the statement that they no longer feel the condition of their bodies and that they attained the martyrdom they had wished for.
source_meta.collection_context_ar: تروي المتحدثة أنهم خُيّروا في رؤية أجساد والديها وأختها بعد تحذيرهم بأن الأجساد مفحمة وربما لا تُعرف. لكنها رفضت ألّا تراهم، لأن والدها ووالدتها وأختها يبقون أهلها مهما كان شكلهم، ولأنها تحمل حسرة سابقة لعدم رؤية إخوتها الشهداء وعدم وداعهم. ثم تصف المشهد بأنه مروع ومخيف ويعجز اللسان عن وصفه. أختها التي كانت في السيارة معهم لم يبق لها أثر واضح وكانت أشلاء وقطعاً بلا ملامح ظاهرة. ووالدتها كان وجهها محروقاً. أما والدها فتتذكره كرجل عظيم صاحب هيبة ووجه جميل، ثم تصدم برؤيته في هذا المنظر. وتختم بالحمد لله وبإعادة تأطير ديني بأنهم لا يشعرون بشكلهم الآن وأنهم نالوا الشهادة التي كانوا يتمنونها.

annotation_meta.selection_policy: Segmentation follows discourse shifts: being warned about the bodies; decision to see them despite fear; hasra over not seeing earlier martyred siblings; viewing the bodies and failing to describe the weapon/effect; description of the sister’s remains; mother’s burned face; father’s remembered dignity contrasted with the altered body; hamd and martyrdom reframing.

approx_context.brief_summary_en: An adult young woman from Gaza City recounts choosing to see the bodies of her parents and sister after being warned that they were charred and possibly unrecognizable. She insists on seeing them because she had not seen or farewelled her previously martyred siblings and did not want to carry the same regret. She describes the scene as horrifying and beyond words, with her sister reduced to unrecognizable fragments, her mother’s face burned, and her father’s dignified living image painfully contrasted with his altered body. The narrative closes with hamd and a martyrdom frame: they do not feel the state of their bodies now, and they attained the shahada they had wished for.
approx_context.brief_summary_ar: تروي شابة بالغة من مدينة غزة أنها اختارت رؤية أجساد والديها وأختها رغم تحذيرها بأن الأجساد مفحمة وربما لا يمكن التعرف عليها. تصر على رؤيتهم لأنها لم ترَ إخوتها الشهداء سابقاً ولم تودّعهم، ولا تريد أن تحمل الحسرة نفسها. تصف المشهد بأنه مروع ويعجز اللسان عن وصفه، حيث كانت أختها أشلاء بلا ملامح واضحة، ووجه والدتها محروقاً، وصورة والدها الحيّ صاحب الهيبة والجمال تصطدم بمنظره بعد الاستشهاد. وتختم بالحمد لله وبإطار الشهادة: هم لا يشعرون بشكل أجسادهم الآن وقد نالوا الشهادة التي تمنوها.

text_en_full: Uh... if you want to see them... so that you know that their bodies are charred and that you may not recognize them, or... so, I mean, do you want to see them or not? They gave us the choice. We told them, I mean, they said to us, 'You will be afraid.' I told them, 'No, I am not afraid. In the end, he is my father. Whatever he is like, I do not want to be afraid.' I did not see my siblings. I did not see them when they were martyrs. I did not farewell them, so I did not want the same thing to happen with my father, my mother, and my sister. Whatever they look like, I want to see them however they are, because it remains a hasra in my heart that I did not see my siblings who were martyred before and did not farewell them. So we went, and we did indeed see them. Of course, the sight was terrifying, frightening. The missiles they fired were missiles... I do not know what to tell you. Yes, internationally prohibited, of course, definitely internationally prohibited, because there was nothing... my sister, my sister who was in the car with them, had no trace at all: pieces, remains, pieces. I mean, her face was not visible, no hand was visible, and no leg was visible. I mean, her appearance was frightening. My mother, her face was burned, I mean burned, burned. I do not understand what they dropped on them that made them like this. My father... I mean, my father, when I see him, he is a great man, with such presence, personality, and a beautiful face. A person, honestly, he was wonderful in appearance. But when I saw him in this state... praise be to Allah, what can one say? In the end, they will not feel how they look. They attained the martyrdom they had wished for.

analysis_note_for_paper.paper_fit_ar: تمثل رواية35 مثالاً شديد الحساسية على قرار رؤية أجساد الشهداء رغم التحذير من تفحمها وعدم إمكانية التعرف عليها. القيمة البحثية هنا ليست فقط في وصف الفقد، بل في منطق الوداع والحسرة: المتحدثة لم ترَ إخوتها الشهداء سابقاً ولم تودعهم، ولذلك تُصر على رؤية والدها ووالدتها وأختها مهما كان شكلهم. يظهر هنا أن الصبر لا يعني غياب الخوف؛ بل يعني تحمل رؤية مشهد مروع لتجنب حسرة أخلاقية/عائلية دائمة. في منتصف الرواية تتكسر اللغة أمام المشهد: «مش عارفة إيش أحكيلك»، مع وصف الأشلاء وغياب الملامح. وفي النهاية تنتقل المتحدثة إلى إطار ديني يحاول تنظيم الألم: «الحمدلله»، «هما مش راح بحسوا في كيف منظرهم»، و«نالوا الشهادة». هذه الرواية مهمة جداً لاختبار النماذج لأنها تحتوي على تعارض عاطفي شديد: رعب بصري، حسرة، حب عائلي، حفظ كرامة الميت، وحمد/شهادة دون أن يعني ذلك اختفاء الصدمة.
analysis_note_for_paper.paper_fit_en: Narrative35 is a highly sensitive example of choosing to view the bodies of martyrs despite warnings that they were charred and potentially unrecognizable. Its research value lies not only in loss description, but in the logic of farewell and hasra: the speaker did not see or farewell her previously martyred siblings, so she insists on seeing her father, mother, and sister regardless of their condition. Sabr here does not mean absence of fear; it means enduring a horrific scene to avoid lifelong moral and familial regret. In the middle of the narrative, language breaks before the visual horror: 'I do not know what to tell you,' followed by descriptions of fragments and absent features. At the end, the speaker shifts into a religious frame that regulates the pain: hamd, the belief that the dead do not feel the state of their bodies, and martyrdom attainment. This narrative is especially valuable for model evaluation because it contains intense affective conflict: visual horror, hasra, family love, preservation of the dignity of the dead, and devotional shahada reframing without erasing trauma.

notes: The narrative contains graphic descriptions of burned and fragmented bodies of close family members.
No personal names appear, but family roles and visual descriptions are highly sensitive.
For public release, avoid images, video stills, faces, exact geolocation, or searchable contextual details.
The phrase 'محرمة دولياً' should be treated as the speaker’s moral/legal framing unless independently verified.
Do not over-normalize hesitation and stuttering; they are important discourse evidence of traumatic speech difficulty.
Do not interpret 'الحمدلله' or 'نالوا الشهادة' as absence of trauma. They function as religious reframing after horror and grief.
This testimony must not be used for individual psychological diagnosis. Analysis should focus on discourse structure, adversity framing, response strategies, contextual markers, and affective signal.
